items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: When I came out I recorded with Coleman Hawkins, and Peggy Lee, Sarah, Ella, Benny again

ctx.x: them and all this but he never got upset, at least I didn't see him get upset, and this way he reminded me a lot of Duke. And he was -- Fletcher was a great writer, you know.

But this was all during this era. Now, after, you know, I told you I went in the army and I stayed for about four years. Of course I did quite a bit of studying there. When I came out I recorded with Coleman Hawkins, and Peggy Lee, Sarah, Ella, Benny again, and there did some nice things. As a matter of fact I worked with Hawk at the Cafe Society Downtown, and which was a very good band, and he was an amazing musician. He was amazing man. He reminded me of a bull in that this man could drink, smoke pot, do…

And probably got off at 4:00 o'clock, he'd drive to Atlantic City. Oh, he was just almost indestructable. I think this contributed to his early death, also, because when he started going he just went, you know, just all at once. He was very quick.
